topic.angle: You use virtually all of your brain

card.title: How much of your brain do you use?

body.question: How much of your brain do you use?
options: Virtually all of it, at different times
body.reveal: The idea that we use only 10% of our brains is a myth. Brain imaging shows activity throughout the brain, and damage almost anywhere has some effect.

probes.question: True or false: people use only about 10% of their brains.

sources.title: Ten percent of the brain myth (Wikipedia)

image_brief.show: A human brain illustration or anatomical drawing

claims.claim: The idea that we use only 10% of our brains is a myth.
claims.quote: Neurologist Barry Gordon refuted the theory

claims.claim: Brain imaging shows activity throughout the brain.
claims.quote: Brain scans have shown that no matter what one is doing, all brain areas are always active

claims.claim: Damage almost anywhere has some effect.
claims.quote: there is almost no area of the brain that can be damaged without loss of abilities

claims.claim: We use virtually all of the brain, at different times.
claims.quote: We use virtually every part of the brain
claims.note: Quote is neurologist Barry Gordon as cited; article adds that some areas are more active at any one time than others.

claims.claim: Probe: people use only about 10% of their brains (false).
claims.quote: The ten-percent-of-the-brain myth states that humans generally use only one-tenth (or some other small fraction) of their brains
claims.note: Article presents this as a myth refuted by Gordon and Beyerstein.
